Simulating decoupled consensus

The test network

  • A Prysm implementation built to test the networking requirements. It sends every object on the wire at its correct size to the other nodes.
  • Primary focus: can finality (FFG) votes be aggregated in time?
  • 500 nodes on DigitalOcean in 8 cities: Amsterdam, Frankfurt, London, Toronto, Santa Clara, Singapore, Bangalore, Sydney.

A note on gossipsub

  • A node forwards a new message to its mesh peers at once (mesh degree D = 8).
  • Every heartbeat (700 ms), the node picks 25% of its other topic peers and sends each an IHAVE with the IDs of the messages it has.
  • The peer replies with IWANT for the messages it does not have.
  • This is naive today: a node asks many peers for the same attestation, and sends the same IHAVE to many peers.
  • The beacon node has no control over IHAVE and IWANT messages.

Staggered publishing vs multiple committees

  • Multiple committees have a nice symmetry: at any time in the slot, FFG votes and aggregates flow in parallel.
  • Multiple committees have more aggregate traffic.
